A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-Transformer work despite the changed title and SGT-to-PPGT renaming. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGT benchmark results, BREC graph-distinguishing results, architectural ablations and sinusoidal-encoding sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds PCQM4Mv2 evaluation, normalization case studies, batch-size sensitivity results and computational-resource measurements.

M1.justification: SGT is renamed PPGT, but AdaRMSN, simplified L2 attention, URPE, RRWP, the shared PE stem and sinusoidal encoding are retained. v2 combines and reorganizes the stem equations; the FFN blocks and sinusoidal component already appear in v1 Section 3.3.

E1.justification: v2 adds PCQM4Mv2 quantum-chemistry graph regression, containing approximately 3.7 million graphs, and a synthetic 2D point-reconstruction task for studying normalization. The original seven prediction datasets and BREC remain, substantially extending the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a 1-WL comparator to BREC and removes plain GatedGCN from the LRGB comparison while retaining GatedGCN+RWSE. Its new PCQM4Mv2 comparison includes previously absent GRPE, TokenGT and virtual-node GCN/GIN variants. The original five-dataset comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include PCQM4Mv2 evaluation without 3D attributes, using the official validation set for testing and a 17.6M-parameter PPGT; 5000-epoch, full-batch autoencoder training; and ZINC batch sizes 4–32 with matched update counts. These are added experimental settings; the retained benchmark hyperparameters in Tables 6–8 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.2–B.4 add a normalization reconstruction case study, a controlled normalization-versus-batch-size analysis, and runtime/memory comparisons with GRIT. The original ZINC architectural ablation remains, and the existing SPE sensitivity study moves from v1 Section 5.5 to v2 Appendix B.1 without changed values.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports a single run for PCQM4Mv2 because of computational constraints. Existing benchmark results retain four runs, seeds 0–3, mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and the same 5% one-tailed t-test for Peptides-func.

E6.justification: v2 adds PCQM4Mv2 MAE 0.0856, normalization and batch-size findings, and resource measurements: PPGT uses 25.07 GB and 100.68 seconds/epoch versus GRIT's 29.16 GB and 141.60 seconds/epoch. Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged. The new BREC no-SPE row contains an inconsistency: total 234 conflicts with category counts summing to 218 and accuracy 54.5%.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D states the GD-WL expressivity relationship and refers to prior work. v2 Appendix E.1 adds Proposition E.1, formal GD-WL definitions, a cited multiset lemma and a constructive attention-based proof under bounded graph size and sufficient heads/layers. The existing normalization-invariance proof is retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that minimal attention, normalization and positional-encoding modifications enable a plain Transformer to achieve strong graph-learning performance and realized expressivity. v2 foregrounds comparisons with higher-order and subgraph GNNs, but these findings and the central contribution already appear in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit quadratic-cost limitations, distinguishes datasets containing many graphs from datasets containing very large graphs, and discusses compatibility limits of potential efficiency techniques in Appendix F. New normalization analyses also connect batch-statistic dependence to BN sensitivity and explain AdaRMSN's stability.

D1.justification: v2 discloses H100 hardware for PCQM4Mv2 and specifies the V100, CPU and model configuration underlying its runtime comparison. Existing initialization rules, feature injection, optimizer choices and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; no code or data release information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for OGB-LSC, TokenGT, GRPE and efficiency techniques including BigBird, Exphormer and GQA, while removing several peripheral citations. It expands discussion of pseudo-coordinates and competing architectures, but retains the central positioning around simplifying graph Transformers.

P1.justification: The title, model name, abstract, preliminaries, method exposition and conclusion are extensively revised. BREC becomes the first experiment, prediction benchmarks are grouped together, SPE receives a separate method subsection, and sensitivity analysis moves into a reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially reflowing and resizing figures and tables. v2 adds PCQM4Mv2 and resource-comparison tables plus two diagnostic figures, expands the BREC table, revises diagram labels and captions, and relocates the existing SPE sensitivity table.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the unchanged proposal: PCQM4Mv2 extends evaluation beyond the original smaller benchmarks, while Appendices B.2–B.4 directly examine magnitude preservation, batch-size sensitivity and computational cost. It also supplies an explicit expressivity argument and clearer scalability limitations. The single-run PCQM4Mv2 evidence and erroneous no-SPE BREC total limit confidence in particular results, but do not outweigh these complementary gains in empirical support and transparency.
